title: The seven performance targets
blurb: Name the seven performance targets, say what each one covers and recognize which target a situation is about.
question: A project board talks about how the new depot will affect local air quality and waste. Which performance target are they discussing?

teach.body: A performance target sets the expected level of success against which the management of the project will be judged. PRINCE2 Project Management, and therefore PRINCE2 Agile, has targets for seven aspects: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. They are the yardsticks the board uses to decide whether the project is on course.

teach.h: The seven targets in plain English
head: Target
What it covers
rows: Measurable improvements the business expects from the change
When it starts, delivers key products and finishes
Products fit for purpose and in line with expectations
What will, and will not, be delivered
How the project affects the wider environment
Limits on the overall risk the project carries
teach.caption: Benefits, quality, scope and sustainability paraphrase book 1.3.2; time, cost and risk follow PRINCE2 7.

teach.body: Under the 'manage by exception' principle, governance works by delegating responsibilities and setting tolerances (limits) for the same seven aspects. The target says what success looks like; the tolerance says how far the project may stray before the next level of management must decide. By default, PRINCE2 Agile sets zero tolerance for extra time and extra cost on all levels of plan.

teach.h: Which target is the discussion about?

teach.body: Corran Bay Transport is replacing its ticket machines. In a board meeting, executive Moira Lindqvist asks for a 10% cut in queuing time with room for more (benefits). Chief product owner Tomasz Wren checks which payment features are in the first release (scope) and that each machine passes accessibility checks (quality). Project manager Kofi Asante confirms the old machines will be recycled responsibly (sustainability).

teach.text: Older material shows six aspects in a 'hexagon'. That is Version 1. PRINCE2 7, and PRINCE2 Agile Version 2, use seven: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Also, a benefit is a measurable improvement, not a product: a new app is an output, the shorter queue is the benefit.

items: A performance target sets the expected success level the management of the project is judged against.
Seven targets: benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk.
Sustainability (impact on the wider environment) is the PRINCE2 7 addition.
Tolerances are set for the same seven aspects under 'manage by exception'.

summary: You can now define a performance target and list all seven. You can also match a situation to the right target, especially separating benefits, quality, scope and sustainability.

A.q: What does a project's performance target set?
options: The order in which the delivery team will build its user stories
The expected success level the project's management is judged against
The roles that make up the project management team structure itself
The set of workshops each process uses to agree the next stage
A.why: A performance target sets the expected success level against which the management of the project will be judged (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Story order is set by prioritization in the backlog, not by a performance target.
whyNot.2: Roles are defined by the organization practice.
whyNot.3: Workshops belong to the processes, not to performance targets.

A.q: Which list gives the seven performance targets in PRINCE2 Project Management?
options: Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability, risk
Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, customer value, risk
Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, change control, risk
Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, team capability, risk
A.why: The seven are benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Customer value is central to agile but is not one of the seven named targets; sustainability is.
whyNot.2: Change control belongs to the issues practice, not to the performance targets.
whyNot.3: Team capability is a people matter (for example the skill matrix), not a performance target.

A.q: Which performance target covers how the project will affect the wider environment?
A.why: Sustainability is how the project will impact the wider environment (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Quality is about products being fit for purpose and meeting expectations.
whyNot.1: Benefits are measurable improvements the business expects from the change.
whyNot.2: Scope is what the project will and will not deliver.

B.q: A board agrees a baseline reduction in staff overtime that the new rota system must achieve, with room to exceed it. Which performance target is this?
B.why: Benefits are measurable improvements the business expects from the change; a baseline improvement with room for more is the benefits target (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Quality concerns whether the rota system's products are fit for purpose.
whyNot.1: Scope concerns which features the system will and will not include.
whyNot.3: Cost concerns the project's own spending, not an improvement in operations.

B.q: A team agrees which reporting features will be delivered and which are out of this project. Which performance target is this about?
B.why: Scope is what the project will deliver and what it will not deliver (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Quality is whether the delivered products are fit for purpose, not which ones are included.
whyNot.2: Benefits are the measurable improvements gained from using the products.
whyNot.3: Time concerns when products are delivered, not which ones.

B.q: Which performance target was added in PRINCE2 7 and is therefore new in PRINCE2 Agile Version 2?
B.why: Sustainability is the seventh target, added by PRINCE2 7; older material shows six aspects.

whyNot.0: Benefits was already one of the six aspects in older material.
whyNot.2: Risk was already one of the six aspects in older material.
whyNot.3: Quality was already one of the six aspects in older material.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Quality is about project products being fit for purpose and in line with expectations.
2. Scope is the measurable improvement the business expects.
3. Tolerances under 'manage by exception' are set for the seven performance aspects.
4. Sustainability is the PRINCE2 Agile name for the cost target.
C.why: Statement 1 is the quality definition (1.3.2); statement 3 matches 'manage by exception', which sets tolerances for all seven aspects (5.2.1.5).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: a measurable improvement is a benefit; scope is what is and is not delivered.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: statement 2 describes benefits and sustainability is its own target.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: sustainability is about the wider environment, not cost.

C.q: A board checks that each delivered kiosk passes its acceptance tests and that recycled materials are used in its casing. Which two targets are being checked?
C.why: Passing acceptance tests is about products being fit for purpose (quality); recycled materials concern impact on the wider environment (sustainability) (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Passing acceptance tests is about fitness for purpose (quality), not about what is in or out of scope.
whyNot.1: Recycled materials concern the wider environment (sustainability), not a measurable business improvement.
whyNot.2: No measurable improvement or project spending is being checked.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Under 'manage by exception', governance works by delegating responsibilities and setting [?] for the seven performance aspects.
C.why: The principle sets tolerances (limits) for benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk (5.2.1.5).

whyNot.1: Baselines are approved versions of products or plans placed under change control; they are not the limits this principle sets.
whyNot.2: Timeboxes are fixed periods for iterations, releases and stages.
whyNot.3: Priorities are set in backlogs, not as the mechanism of this principle.

reteach.title: Seven dials on the dashboard
reteach.question: How can you remember the seven targets and tell the similar ones apart?

blocks.h: Count them on one hand and two fingers

blocks.body: Is it an improvement the business gains? Benefits. Is it about products being fit for purpose? Quality. Is it about what is in or out? Scope. Is it about the wider environment? Sustainability.

blocks.text: Six aspects belong to Version 1. If an option lists six, or replaces sustainability with something else, it is out of date.

explain.body: A performance target sets the expected success level against which the management of the project will be judged (1.3.2).

test.q: Against what is the management of a project judged in PRINCE2 Project Management?
test.why: Performance targets set the success level the management of the project is judged against (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Velocity is a team measure used for forecasting, not the basis of judging project management.
whyNot.2: The lessons log records lessons, not success levels.
whyNot.3: Stage boundaries are decision points, not success measures.

explain.body: Benefits, cost, time, quality, scope, sustainability and risk. Sustainability is the PRINCE2 7 addition.

test.q: Which of these is one of the seven performance targets?
test.why: Sustainability is one of the seven targets (1.3.2).

whyNot.0: Velocity is an agile measure of work completed per iteration.
whyNot.1: Value drives agile prioritization but is not one of the seven named targets.
whyNot.3: Transparency is a characteristic of the agile mindset.

explain.body: Benefits: measurable improvements the business expects from the change. Quality: characteristics that make products fit for purpose and in line with expectations.

test.q: A board measures whether a new website reduces phone calls by a fifth. Which performance target is this?
test.why: Fewer calls is a measurable improvement the business expects: a benefit (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Quality would be whether the website itself is fit for purpose.
whyNot.2: Scope would be which pages or features are included.
whyNot.3: Sustainability would be the effect on the wider environment.

explain.body: How the project will impact the wider environment (1.3.2). It sits beside the other six targets and has its own tolerance.

test.q: A team must keep the carbon footprint of a new warehouse below an agreed level. Which performance target applies?
test.why: Impact on the wider environment is the sustainability target (1.3.2).

whyNot.1: Scope concerns what will and will not be delivered.
whyNot.2: Quality concerns products being fit for purpose.
